Patch 0.41.0.18 (the last bell opens the way)

  • The deep halls finally answer a cleared room: defeating the last living enemy assigned to an encounter now advances authoritative room progression, pays the established room reward once, and opens the next objective instead of leaving the route frozen.
  • A fleeing monster cannot confuse the chamber: room ownership follows each enemy's server spawn cohort, so pulling a foe into a corridor or later arena neither clears the wrong room nor strands its original encounter.
  • Treasure stays on the side of the threshold where it fell: dungeon loot now retains its instance ID, keeping drops visible and collectible by the party instead of silently placing them in the overworld scope.
  • The chosen run level reaches the whole reward loop: dungeon trash, elites, and bosses now carry their selected run level into XP and level-qualified loot rules as well as the stat multipliers they already used.
  • Every chamber shows what the server knows: current rooms breathe with a quiet inner ward, live objectives raise a rotating ritual crown, completed encounters settle into a pale clear sigil, and chest, shrine, and ambush seals disappear only after their authoritative reward state advances.
  • The entrance remembers the road home: each dungeon's generated threshold now holds a dim return aperture throughout the run and kindles it brightly when the server reports no objective remaining.
  • Four bosses break the floor in four tongues: Thorncrypt Root Quake grows an inward briar ring, Furnace Rupture fractures into molten fault bars, Stormbreak binds a lightning hex, and Undertow Crush closes in as concentric tide circles.
  • Danger fields keep their exact promise: all regional boss motifs sit inside the unchanged server radius and duration; the outer boundary remains the precise area that can damage the player.
  • Spell warnings no longer impersonate bosses: player-created delayed impacts carry ordinary impact danger metadata, while actual dungeon boss slams receive their named boss tier from the server.
  • Warning names remain readable while they pulse: telegraph animation now preserves the label's authored width and dynamically fits longer encounter names instead of collapsing them to a one-unit square or clipping their first letters.
  • The encounter contract is inspectable: new server regressions cover last-enemy room clears, cross-room isolation, run-level propagation, instance-scoped loot, and regional boss metadata; deterministic hardware-Chrome galleries cover every room lifecycle and all four damaging boss fields.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-18.

Patch 0.41.0.17 (the deep halls remember their names)

  • Four thresholds now lead to four different worlds: the Thorncrypt, Furnace Below, Shattered Aerie, and Drowned Sanctum replace their shared cobblestone rooms with generated burial masonry, broken obsidian, storm-slate conductors, and drowned basalt.
  • The floor tells you what waits ahead: entry gates, treasure caches, restorative shrines, ambush chambers, boss approaches, elite guards, boss lairs, and route halls each receive a readable ritual layout driven by the server's room metadata.
  • Thorncrypt roots wake beneath the dead: mossed blocks, winding grave roots, witchlight wards, bronze vigils, and root-bound waystones carry the Verdant Bastion's identity through every room.
  • The Furnace Below cracks but does not cool: staggered black-glass plates, branching magma faults, crucible fangs, iron pylons, and ember seals turn the Molten Core into an ancient working forge.
  • The Shattered Aerie binds a storm underfoot: offset slate, silver circuits, captive sky nodes, floating fragments, and violet shrine light distinguish Tempest rooms at a glance.
  • The Drowned Sanctum keeps the tide's last oath: flooded basalt, luminous tide marks, coral antlers, moonlit fonts, and black-water circles shape the Abyssal Well.
  • Dungeon atmosphere finally follows the dungeon: instance identity now selects light, fog, exposure, bloom, and ambient particles, fixing all four remote-coordinate interiors incorrectly inheriting the Air realm preset.
  • Transitions shed the old weather cleanly: entering or leaving an instance immediately retires the previous realm's particles, while shared generated geometry, materials, and texture maps dispose once when the scene changes.
  • The server still owns every step: canonical room and corridor dimensions, forty-unit doors, fifteen-unit walls, collision boxes, walkable rectangles, spawn positions, combat, rewards, and room progression are unchanged; new dressing is visual-only.
  • The old dungeon texture queue is gone: all four generated interiors start synchronously without requesting the legacy cobblestone floor or wall images.
  • Every deep-hall beat is inspectable: exact-geometry unit coverage and a deterministic hardware-Chrome gallery render all four surface families and all eight room identities at High and Low quality.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-02-17.

Patch 0.41.0.16 (four doors dream in four tongues)

  • The Thorncrypt grows its own crown: the Verdant Bastion threshold is now a root-bound fortress with mossed ramparts, witchlight slits, funeral bronze, antler branches, and a bright briar gate.
  • The Furnace Below opens its iron throat: the Molten Core becomes an obsidian kiln flanked by crucible pylons, chained horns, basalt fangs, and molten channels that lead cleanly to its portal.
  • The Shattered Aerie catches the storm: the Tempest Spire rises as a narrow broken needle of floating slate, silver conductors, violet arcs, and a captive sky-eye.
  • The Drowned Sanctum watches from below: the Abyssal Well is now a low tide altar with a black-water eye, coral antlers, anchor-tentacles, moon pearls, and a drowned reliquary door.
  • Every old footprint remains exact: all four generated roots preserve the measured production width, height, depth, grounding, world coordinate, circular blocker, interaction radius, click target, and authoritative dungeon ID.
  • Entry logic never changed hands: hover hints, eligibility requests, level gates, party rules, instance creation, transition cleanup, exit routing, and server authority remain on their established paths.
  • Moving targets stay beneath the cursor: eligible canvas pointer samples now resolve hover against the camera and actor hitbox in the same input turn, preventing reconciliation or enemy motion from turning an exact hostile click into stale ground; the existing 20 Hz budget still caps raycast work.
  • Distant doors arrive immediately: overworld thresholds are created synchronously from cached geometry, removing the model-download queue and its potential late-attach window.
  • One hundred nine details travel in thirty-four batches: each production landmark is merged by regional material, keeping the four ornate silhouettes bounded to eight or nine visible draw submissions apiece.
  • The authored-model ledger reaches zero: the final four GLBs—70,429,592 bytes—have left production code, manifests, preloads, caches, and the repository; all 106 authored models from the migration baseline are now gone.
  • The thresholds are inspectable: exact-contract unit tests and a dedicated hardware-Chrome gallery cover all four themes at High and Low quality while rejecting every authored-model request.
  • The settings screen tells the truth: dungeon thresholds now appear as built-in procedural art with no 71 MB download button, and cache generation advances to 2026-09-02-16.

Patch 0.41.0.15 (Lanternhold keeps the long vigil)

  • A real silhouette crowns the safe road: Lanternhold's northern hall is now a many-gabled oathhouse with layered masonry, black-oak framing, amber windows, grave-road buttresses, a broken-sun belfry, and a tall slate vigil spire.
  • Every service owns its corner of town: the eastern votive market, western Ashen Smithy, Gilded Compact auction hall, Oathfire Forge, and Wayfarer Reliquary each receive a distinct code-generated structure instead of an imported or fallback shell.
  • Fifteen camps remember where they stood: outer-town pilgrim vigils now combine faceted tents, oathfires, bedrolls, standards, and way-lanterns in a deterministic layout that keeps the existing fifty-unit town clearing and twenty-unit camp spacing.
  • The paths have not moved: all seven generated families carry explicit invisible gameplay boxes measured from the production-scaled models they replace, preserving collision, grounding, click targets, service range, landmark placement, and navigation.
  • Lanternhold arrives before distant doors: generated buildings and camps are constructed beside foliage immediately, no longer waiting behind the remaining dungeon-facade download queue.
  • One town, fifteen materials: ten cached faceted geometries and a restrained charcoal timber, old stone, iron, brass, blood-cloth, amber, spirit, and oathfire palette keep the settlement cohesive without rebuilding resources per structure.
  • The whole vigil travels in thirty-eight calls: landmarks are merged by material and all fifteen camps share nine instanced batches, reducing the settlement from 390 visible mesh submissions to 38 before service props.
  • Late packets no longer pull ghosts backward: remote movement now carries extrapolated overshoot into a bounded, continuous reconciliation instead of snapping a character backward when the next authoritative transform arrives.
  • A swing begins where the server can honor it: basic-attack clicking, chase distance, client validation, and the authoritative class ranges now agree at 4m for Fighter/Cleric and 16m for Rogue/Wizard, including large-target reach.
  • The old town leaves no weight behind: seven superseded GLBs totaling 176.75 MB have left production code, preload lists, caches, and the repository; only four authored dungeon facades totaling 70.43 MB remain in the migration ledger.
  • The vigil is inspectable: unit coverage audits every identity piece, exact bound, cache, placement, shadow, and loader route, while hardware Chrome renders the complete settlement at High and Low quality and rejects any authored-model request.
  • Caches follow the new skyline: the asset generation advances to 2026-09-02-15 so existing clients retire the prior town-model cache cleanly.

Patch 0.41.0.14 (one oath across every edge)

  • Every release now arrives as one world: the published entry script, full JavaScript module graph, stylesheet imports, and local CSS resources receive the exact commit identity, preventing a new page from mixing with four-hour-old edge-cached game logic.
  • The gate verifies the runtime, not only the label: deployment waits until production serves both the expected release manifest and the commit-versioned main module before any live character is allowed into the verification run.
  • Live QA walks through a fresh doorway: production browser checks open the commit-qualified document, so edge propagation is tested against the release being approved rather than whichever anonymous HTML object a regional cache remembers.
  • Old groves fade without breaking travelers: three 155–157 byte empty glTF migration bridges answer stale pre-procedural tree requests without restoring any authored geometry, download weight, collision, or runtime dependency.
  • Asset caches turn a clean page: the cache generation advances to 2026-09-02-14, old generations are retired on activation, and service-worker updates bypass the HTTP cache so future migrations cannot remain pinned behind an obsolete worker import.
  • The wilds remain wholly generated: the nine realm-specific foliage families, 840 deterministic instances, exact 65-hazard clearings, ten shared geometries, twenty-eight materials, and 59.93 MB authored-model reduction from 0.41.0.13 remain unchanged.

Patch 0.41.0.13 (the wild remembers every realm)

  • Nine wild silhouettes replace three old trees: every overworld realm now has its own code-generated foliage families instead of sharing randomly scattered imported birch, pine, and willow models.
  • Gloamwood keeps its grave rites: pale ossuary birch, black grave pine, and votive mourning willow carry scarred bark, funeral tiers, moss, and small grave-lantern fruit.
  • Moonfrost grows beneath drowned light: rime pines layer ice and snow around conduction crystals, while silver-reed willows suspend cold spirit fruit over dark trunks.
  • The Cinder Wastes grows teeth: forked corpsewood burns around contained ember hearts, and basalt briars cage restrained magma in rusted volcanic thorns.
  • Stormcrown bends but does not break: gale cypress leans beneath storm conductors and captive lightning rises from angular slate-and-silver crystal growths.
  • Eight hundred forty plants, only ten geometries: reusable per-part instancing and twenty-eight cached materials keep all nine families lightweight, stable, and consistent across reconnects.
  • Danger stays readable: foliage clearings exactly track all 65 server-authored permanent hazard coordinates and radii, then add an eight-unit visibility apron around every lava pool, sandstorm, lightning field, and wind shear.
  • Routes stay clean: Lanternhold, every dungeon entrance, cardinal roads, and gateway sightlines remain open; only Gloamwood retains tree collision, so new realm dressing cannot silently alter combat paths.
  • The realms arrive sooner: generated foliage appears immediately while remaining legacy town and dungeon architecture streams in separately.
  • Release protection no longer collides with class magic: the allowlisted gameplay matrix keeps its bounded inspection shield separate from Teleport Phase and short class invulnerability windows, so testing one rune cannot expose the character—or a retry—to unrelated hostile damage.
  • Moving targets stay alive under the cursor: hover selection now follows creatures beneath a stationary pointer at a steady refresh rate, every click samples its exact coordinates, and actors raycast through one lightweight proxy instead of every piece of an animated rig.
  • Smaller download, durable proof: 59.93 MB of obsolete plant GLBs left production routes, while unit coverage and a hardware-Chrome gallery validate every family, transform, cache, placement, collider rule, and hazard clearing.

Patch 0.41.0.12 (the rootbound procession wakes)

  • The Thorncrypt has four true wardens: Rootbound Warden, Briar Matron, Rustbound Colossus, and Hollow Sentinel are now distinct code-generated boss rigs in root-bound stone, tarnished bronze, dead ivy, bone, and restrained witchlight.
  • An ossuary gate learned to walk: the Rootbound Warden bears grave plates, a crown of roots, funerary ivy, orbiting crypt shards, and a witchlit gate maul.
  • The Matron opens her sepulchre: layered dead petals, an eleven-spined crown, thorn halo, ritual shards, and crescent briar sickle create a narrow but dangerous caster silhouette.
  • The rusted procession marches: the Colossus is a broad bronze reliquary of armor slabs, luminous rivets, funeral pipes, and a two-handed procession hammer.
  • One last light guards the hollow: the final Sentinel exposes an empty rib cage around a green soul, trailing vigil tatters beneath a high crown and long poleblade.
  • Twenty boss performances replace twenty files: every boss owns generated Idle, Walk, Run, Attack, and stable Death motion with actor-owned pose reset and cached immutable render resources.
  • Boss rules remain exact: the established 2, 1.5, 3, and 2.5-unit combat radii, Rootbound attack timing, room order, scaling, rewards, daily credit, death, cleanup, and replication are unchanged.
  • Guardian Roar recognizes every generation: its offline fallback no longer relies on an obsolete seven-enemy allowlist; current and future hostile actors are taunted while players, the Seraph, and service NPCs stay friendly.
  • Moving enemies stay under your cursor: procedural hostiles gain a narrow input-only latency allowance around their visible bounds, preventing a freshly acquired live target from becoming a ground click without changing combat or damage radii.
  • Lighter art and faster releases: 95.08 MB of obsolete boss GLBs left every runtime route, and self-hosted browser gates no longer restore a redundant 3.7 GB dependency cache before their locked install.
  • Reconnect QA sees the living runtime clearly: the two-client browser gate now proves the observer is error-free before its intentional reload, discards only teardown cancellations from that abandoned document, and continues auditing the reconstructed session.

Patch 0.41.0.11 (the drowned moon finds its choir)

  • Moonfrost has its own monsters now: Mountain Trolls, Aqua Golems, Sirens, and Frost Guardians are four purpose-built code-generated rigs sharing bone, dark iron, drowned teal, pale ice, and restrained aurora light—not recolors of one body.
  • The rimeback comes down from the pass: Mountain Trolls carry a fur mantle, jagged ice ridge, cairn club, tusks, and a dangling aurora charm across a broad, hunched silhouette.
  • The drowned cairns remember the tide: Aqua Golems combine waterlogged stone, barnacles, tide drips, a captive sea-soul, and a grave-anchor into a heavy shoreline guardian.
  • A dead choir sings beneath the ice: Sirens float in split drowned shrouds with exposed bone strings, crown spines, voice chimes, spectral notes, talons, and a silver crescent blade.
  • The pale vigil tolls: Frost Guardians wear glacial plate around an aurora heart, broken back-halo, horned visor, vigil bell, and ice-bladed polearm.
  • Twenty distinct motions replace twenty files: Each creature receives generated Idle, Walk, Run, Attack, and stable Death performances with actor-owned limbs, implements, accents, and pose reset for local and replicated enemies.
  • New forms, exact old rules: All four retain their authoritative 1.25-unit combat radius plus existing level bands, movement, pursuit, attacks, loot, XP, daily-quest credit, elite rules, overworld spawns, and Drowned Sanctum uses.
  • Readable from feet to crown: Explicit grounded selection bounds cover every ridge, veil, halo, anchor, club, and polearm without coupling visible size to combat reach or multiplying pooled hitboxes.
  • Proven in motion and stripped from production: Unit and hardware-Chrome galleries validate finite transforms, shared caches, independent poses, all states, local/remote pairs, and High/Low quality. Twenty obsolete GLBs—152.04 MB—left all runtime routes and the deployed asset tree while remaining recoverable through Git history.

Patch 0.41.0.10 (the choir keeps its stride)

  • Spirit Guardians no longer steals your destination: The Cleric's signature aura now always resolves at its caster, even when the cursor happens to cross a distant creature during a right-click cast.
  • Movement and casting stay independent: Activating the aura while running preserves the ordinary click-to-move path, speed, state, and prediction history instead of silently converting the cast into a target chase and stopping on arrival.
  • The server receives unambiguous intent: Self-casts now send the Cleric's current position with no target ID; damage radius, mana, cooldown, duration, runes, and server authority are unchanged.
  • Production found it; coverage keeps it: A dedicated regression test casts through a hostile hover while moving and proves the path survives, alongside the existing movement, authority, ability, and live four-class browser matrices.

Patch 0.41.0.9 (the graves ring, the furnace wakes)

  • The Gloamwood has built a body for its dead: Constructs are now code-generated grave-reliquaries made from cairn stone, grasping roots, moss, funeral brass, and a caged soul instead of an imported character set.
  • Every relic tells the same rite: A tolling stone maul, swinging grave bell, marked cairn joints, funerary mask, and root crown give the Construct a broad, readable silhouette related to—but unmistakable from—the ossuary pilgrim.
  • The Wastes' furnace walks: Inferno Titans become towering crucible giants with obsidian anatomy, a white-hot caged core, shoulder vents, molten crown, caldera cleaver, and chained ash censer.
  • Weight lives in the motion: Both enemies receive independent generated Idle, Walk, Run, Attack, and stable Death performances. Limbs, masks, weapons, bells, censers, jaws, and complete bodies move through actor-owned pivots for local and replicated creatures.
  • New silhouettes, unchanged combat: Spawn sectors, daily-quest credit, aggro, pursuit, attacks, health, damage, loot, XP, elite rules, death, respawn, and network authority stay on their existing paths. The established 2.5-unit Construct and 1-unit Inferno Titan combat radii are preserved exactly.
  • Selection follows the whole creature: Grounded procedural bounds cover roots, crowns, vents, implements, and each giant frame without accumulating stale hitboxes or coupling visual size to combat reach.
  • Rendered, not merely asserted: Tests exercise every state for finite transforms, independent pose ownership, immutable shared resources, exact combat and interaction dimensions, explicit routing, loader bypass, and pool safety; hardware Chrome captures both families at High and Low quality.
  • Forty-three more megabytes reforged as code: Ten superseded Construct and Inferno Titan GLBs—43.38 MB—have left production manifests, preload routes, fallbacks, and the deployed asset tree while remaining recoverable through Git history.
